clue.text: Bishop, say, identified as liable to drop things

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
to say something is to utter it
to finger a suspect is to identify them to the police

explanation.surface: A clergyman has been named as the clumsy one who keeps dropping things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop, say' reads as one example phrase, but it splits: 'Bishop' gives B and 'say' gives UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone clumsy, whose grip slips as if their hands were greased, is said to have buttery fingers.

clue.text: Battered woman kept in bed

definitions.meaning: a woman beaten so that she has a bruised eye, named Susan here
a yellow daisy-like flower grown in a garden bed

explanation.definitionFit: The name of a cottage-garden flower reads literally as a woman with bruised eyes.

clue.text: Most of the fibre is for a Scottish order

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter, so the word the loses its end

parts.note: istle is a tough plant fibre from Mexican agave, used for cords and brushes

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain textile is reserved for a Scottish honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' trims THE to TH. ISTLE (also spelt ixtle) is an uncommon word for a plant fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Most Ancient and Most Noble Order of the Thistle is Scotland's highest order of chivalry, named after its national flower.

clue.text: Time's not on our side

parts.note: the saying that time is against us, read as naming what time is: a foe, one who is on the other side

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that the clock is against us.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe is by definition not on our side, and proverbially time is one.

clue.text: Latitude drawn without using instruments

definitions.meaning: freedom of action, as when one is given carte blanche
sketched by hand alone, with no ruler or compasses

explanation.definitionFit: Being allowed to act unhindered, and drawing unaided by tools, share the same two-word phrase.

clue.text: Snooping, but not out to turn informer

parts.note: no is a word meaning not, as in 'no better'
to sing is slang for confessing or informing to the police

explanation.surface: Someone poking around, though without meaning to grass anyone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Poking one's nose into other people's business is prying.

clue.text: Government agent who took duties seriously

definitions.text: Government agent who took duties seriously

parts.words: Government agent who took duties seriously
parts.note: 'took duties' reads as being conscientious, but means collecting taxes levied on goods for the state

explanation.definitionFit: An officer of the old Board of Excise collected duties on goods such as spirits and tobacco.

clue.text: Charm of English university in Roman complex

indicators.note: the university letter is placed inside the rearranged letters
complex here means intricate or muddled, so the letters of the word are tangled up

explanation.surface: Describes the attraction of an English college within a Roman building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges ROMAN to NAMOR, and 'in' puts U inside it to make NAMOUR after E.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate someone is to fill them with love; the verb is mostly used as 'enamoured of'.

clue.text: Person carrying newspaper first to show prominent leader

indicators.note: first says the newspaper's name comes ahead of the carrier

parts.note: the Standard is a London newspaper, the Evening Standard
a bearer is a person who carries something

explanation.surface: A paperboy holding the paper up first to show off a famous leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the one carrying the flag at the head of an army, hence any figurehead of a movement.

clue.text: Animation of a learner I have taken to head

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate letter
I've is the contraction of I have
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A drama student being bright and lively after taking it into their head.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS, a headland, appears in Scottish place names such as Loch Ness's neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means liveliness, the state of being full of life.

clue.text: For example, pottery vessel

definitions.meaning: pottery is one instance of a skilled handicraft

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a handicraft skill and a boat.

clue.text: Little Catherine is in the pool

definitions.meaning: a pet form of the name Catherine
a shared pot of money, as in a card game

explanation.definitionFit: A pet name for Catherine is also a fund pooled by players.

clue.text: Bananas reduced in price without trouble

parts.note: a bunch of bananas growing together is called a hand
prices that are down have been cut

explanation.surface: A shopper notes that the bananas are cheaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like an anagram signal, but it is fodder: a cluster of bananas is a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning easily is winning effortlessly, from a jockey who could drop his hands and relax.

clue.text: Producing elastic

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both giving forth a harvest and giving way when pressed.

clue.text: Timeless character of medic with international medical group

parts.note: a doctor is a medic
WHO is the World Health Organization

explanation.surface: Describes a classic figure, a physician working with a global health body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' plays on the BBC character being a Time Lord who travels freely through time.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running BBC science-fiction hero is a time-travelling alien, so beyond the reach of time.

clue.text: Customer taking part in code of silence

indicators.note: part in says the answer is a portion of the words around it, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A shopper joining in with a vow of secrecy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia's rule forbids members from talking to the police about crimes.

clue.text: The conclusions one was looking for?

definitions.text: The conclusions one was looking for?

parts.words: The conclusions one was looking for?
parts.note: a report's conclusions, read literally as things discovered after searching

explanation.definitionFit: An inquiry's results are what it has discovered, and things discovered are what a searcher wanted.

clue.text: Cut off many a head over time

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, so many

indicators.note: over here means the time letter is placed across, inside the pair

parts.note: each means per head, as in 'a pound each'

explanation.surface: Beheading many a victim over a period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts T inside EACH to make ETACH, after D.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate or remove something is to sever it.

clue.text: Instant shine

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in 'in the twinkling of an eye'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a split second and a glimmer of light.

clue.text: Knight in victory due to be screened

indicators.note: the knight letter is placed inside the word for victory

parts.note: a win is a victory
N is the chess notation for knight
owed means due to be paid

explanation.surface: A knight who has won and is now due to appear on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain is sifted from chaff by blowing air through it, and to screen is to sift.

clue.text: Form of surveillance in West Indies father set up

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, so read from the bottom

parts.note: pater is Latin, and old schoolboy slang, for father

explanation.surface: A Caribbean father who planted a listening device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns PATER into RETAP below WI.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugging a telephone line is a way of secretly listening in.

clue.text: Early form of life found more by accident

indicators.note: accident, after the fodder, says the letters fall into place randomly, so they are scrambled

explanation.surface: Finding more of a primitive organism purely by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism in its first stage of development before birth or hatching.

clue.text: Dressed for action, out of shape unit going in

indicators.note: says the unit letter is put inside the word for shapeless

parts.note: unformed means without shape
I is the Roman numeral one, a unit

explanation.surface: A soldier dressed for battle, though the unit is unfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of shape' looks like an anagram signal for 'unit'; it is the synonym UNFORMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers and police on duty wear prescribed clothing, so are kitted out for action.

clue.text: American type on drug is uncannily frightening

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after the drug letter

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
the Erie were a Native American people of the Lake Erie region

explanation.surface: A Yank on ecstasy who is unnervingly spooky.
explanation.definitionFit: Weird and unsettling, as a ghostly silence is.

clue.text: Ending of poem representative read out

indicators.note: read out says the word is spoken, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomatic representative

explanation.surface: A diplomat reading the final verse of a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The short closing stanza of a ballade, addressed to a patron, is its formal send-off.

clue.text: Query two points given in biased fashion

parts.note: to query is to ask
E is east, a compass point
W is west, a second compass point

explanation.surface: Asking about a couple of debating points made unfairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two points' are two compass directions, east and west.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked or awry, so skewed or slanted.

clue.text: One who repairs to gambling centre to get gold without tax

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the gold sits beyond the tax

parts.note: Reno is a Nevada city famous for its casinos
VAT is value added tax
or is heraldic gold

explanation.surface: Someone heading to a casino town to win gold free of tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who restores buildings or objects to good condition.

clue.text: Fan of Leander?

parts.note: in Greek myth Leander loved the priestess Hero and swam the Hellespont nightly to reach her; the query hints that he, not some admirer of his, is the fan

explanation.walkthrough: Leander drowned swimming to his beloved, whose name was Hero, so he literally adored Hero.
explanation.definitionFit: An idoliser of a great person; Leander, adoring the woman named Hero, fits it literally.
